thread:
maria-cs: ACME reports that their mobile app is getting truncated JSON chunks from our streaming JSON endpoint. Client shows "Unexpected end of JSON input" when parsing. They attached a minimal curl from their mobile network.

customer_acme: Repro command we ran from the device (they use curl on Android debug shell):
```bash
curl --http2 -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-4o-stream&mode=json"
```
Last chunk we got ends like:
```
data: {"id":"resp_42","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Looks like the sentence gets cut off here and doesn't finish the last word"}
```
parser: Unexpected end of JSON input on client.

eng-chris: Thanks. Two quick diagnostics: 1) force curl --http1.1 to rule out HTTP/2 behavior; 2) try wifi vs carrier to rule out middlebox. Also need full curl -i output (headers) and any edge trace ids. If it's HTTP/2-only, could be RST from client or middlebox.

customer_acme: We did --http1.1 and it completed fine. On wifi it succeeds; on carrier network it fails. No 401/permission errors in server logs. We'll collect the raw -i output and the last bytes.

sre-priya: Edge traces for the failing session:
```
[edge] 2026-03-17T14:40:12Z id=ez-221 client=172.18.5.9 stream_id=87 upstream=svc-inference-07 "upstream prematurely closed connection" proto=HTTP/2 RST_STREAM code=0x8
[edge] 2026-03-17T14:40:12Z id=ez-221 trace=tx-331 sess=acme_mobile token_id=tok-acme9
```
RST_STREAM 0x8 is CANCEL. Pattern: mobile network or SDK aborting long-lived HTTP/2 streams.

devex-jamie: Follow-up: our mobile SDK had a token refresh flow that used to call request.cancel() on any in-flight request when renewing tokens. That will generate a client-side RST and produce truncated SSE payloads for long streams. We pushed a change on the mobile branch to make refresh non-destructive for streaming endpoints: mark stream sockets as "draining" and open new streams with refreshed token. Patch excerpt:
```diff
- if (auth.needsRefresh) req.cancel();
+ if (auth.needsRefresh) { if (!req.isStreaming) req.cancel(); else req.markDraining = true; }
```
This avoids mid-stream aborts.

eng-chris: Short-term workarounds for customers: 1) force HTTP/1.1 when possible; 2) disable aggressive auto-refresh on mobile during active streams; 3) test on wifi or different carrier. Long-term: SDK release + a gateway tolerance change to treat midstream 401/refresh as non-fatal for SSE streams if connection otherwise healthy.

maria-cs: I'll send ACME instructions: try v2.4.0-beta of mobile SDK (staging) or run on wifi and report results. Also ask for tcpdump from device and the exact last bytes of the chunk for correlation.

deploy-bot: devex/mobile-sdk@v2.4.0-beta published to npm and staging Play store. Release notes: "Avoid aborting active streaming requests on token refresh; mark as draining instead." CI job linked: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/mobile-sdk/456

customer_acme: Installing v2.4.0-beta now on staging device. We'll test on carrier network and wifi, will upload logs and tcpdump if still failing. Thanks!

sre-priya: As a temporary server-side debug step, we're enabling verbose edge logging for RST_STREAM CANCEL events for the next 2 hours and extending trace retention for affected ids so we can correlate with tcpdump. If you get the last 64 bytes of the last SSE event, send them here.

eng-chris: If the issue persists after the SDK fix, we'll look for middlebox FIN behavior or HTTP/2 proxy timeouts on the carrier path. Also consider adding a small keepalive ping for very long SSE streams on mobile to keep some middleboxes from considering the connection idle.

maria-cs: Ack — I'll coordinate tests with ACME and update this thread. :thumbsup:
